summary.short: Creates the Innovation in Artificial Intelligence Grant Pilot Program, administered by the office subject to available funds. Business entities may receive grants to develop a practical AI course with a public or private school for kindergarten-through-twelfth-grade students and prepare them for technology careers. No start date stated.
summary.long: Part 13 of Utah Senate Bill 84 enacts Sections 63N-3-1301 and 63N-3-1302. It defines business entity (a for-profit or nonprofit organization), pilot program, and student (a child enrolled in a public or private school, grades kindergarten through twelfth grade). It creates the Innovation in Artificial Intelligence Grant Pilot Program, administered by the office subject to the availability of funds. The purpose is to award a grant to a business entity to develop a program, material, and curriculum that teaches an AI course to students with an emphasis on practical training and prepares students for technology careers. A grantee must work in partnership with a public or private school. Applications must describe the proposal, the school partnership, and any partnerships with other entities. The office considers the likelihood the proposal achieves the purpose and its overall viability. Before receiving funds, a grantee must enter a written agreement with the office specifying the grant amount and the distribution period and structure. The office may make rules under the Utah Administrative Rulemaking Act on application criteria, awards, and grantee reporting. The office must include an annual written update on the pilot in the report under Section 63N-1a-306. The excerpt contains no penalties, enforcement provisions, or start date.

events.note: The fetched text contains no dates. It gives no enactment, signature, publication or entry-into-force date, and no application or deadline date for the pilot program. Grant administration is 'subject to the availability of funds' (63N-3-1302(1)). The annual written update in 63N-3-1302(7) is a recurring reporting duty without a stated date, so it is not coded as an event here.

thresholds.note: The text sets no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. The 'student' definition (kindergarten through twelfth grade, 63N-3-1301(3)) is a scope definition by school grade level, not a numeric threshold. The grant amount is left to the written agreement under 63N-3-1302(5)(a), and funding depends on 'the availability of funds' (63N-3-1302(1)), so no value is stated.
